title: Trade-Bot quality and security requirements registry
description: Structural and cross-field contract for config/quality_registry.json. The conditional rules below (status vs verification, status vs planned_in, id prefix vs kind, critical vs waiver) used to live only in src/quality/registry.py, which meant any tool that read the registry without importing that module -- a deploy step, an editor, a review bot -- saw a file that looked valid and was not. They are expressed here so the JSON enforces itself. What remains in the loader is only what JSON Schema genuinely cannot express: whether a named test exists on disk, whether depends_on resolves, and whether the dependency graph is acyclic.

kind_definitions.description: What each kind of entry asserts. The id prefix is bound to the kind by the conditional rules in definitions/entry.

test_types.description: The test taxonomy of docs/quality/TEST_STRATEGY.md: type -> the question it answers.

phases.description: PR-NNN -> the phase title it delivers. Every planned or partial entry names one of these.

statement.description: The requirement as a testable proposition, not a slogan.

source.description: Section of docs/Quality-Engineering this entry comes from, e.g. 'QE-42'.

failure_mode.description: What goes wrong in production if this requirement is violated. Required, because an entry nobody can describe the failure of is one nobody can size the priority of -- but deliberately not length-policed beyond a token: 'Money leaves.' is a better failure mode than most paragraphs, and a minimum that punishes terse writing teaches padding.

allOf.title: A verified or partial entry names at least one test
allOf.description: Status is a claim about evidence. 'Verified' with an empty verification array is the failure this registry exists to prevent -- a requirement that reports green because nobody wrote the test.

allOf.title: A planned entry names no test and does name a phase
allOf.description: Planned means the work has an owner and no evidence yet. A planned entry carrying a verification is a claim with nothing behind it; one with no planned_in is work nobody has scheduled.

allOf.title: A partial entry names the phase that will finish it
A verified entry names no phase
allOf.description: planned_in on a verified entry is a leftover from before it shipped, and it makes the 'outstanding work by phase' table lie.

allOf.title: An accepted gap carries a waiver and no phase
allOf.description: A gap with no waiver is an undocumented decision; a waiver with no expiry is a permanent hole, which is why definitions/waiver requires review_by.

allOf.title: A critical requirement can never be an accepted gap
allOf.description: To waive it you must first argue, in the diff, that it is not critical. That argument is the control.

allOf.title: The id prefix and the kind are one fact: INV- is an invariant
Every other prefix is a requirement

test.description: Repo-relative path to a test file, optionally ::-qualified to a node. Existence is checked by the loader -- a renamed test must turn the claim red rather than silently passing.

review_by.description: ISO date. A waiver with no expiry is a permanent hole.
